findings.claim: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the group vanished from the DB, breaking the documented never-null GroupModel contract; the NPE moves downstream instead of being fixed.
findings.evidence: server-spi/.../GroupModel.java:296 '@return The number of groups beneath this group. Never returns {@code null}.' Null flows via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (GroupUtils.java:90) into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount; admin UI GroupPickerDialog.tsx:324,379 checks subGroupCount !== 0, so a deleted group renders as having children; any SPI extension unboxing the Long gets an NPE. Codebase precedent for vanished source is an empty/zero fallback (DefaultLazyLoader, CachedGroup.getRoleMappings -> emptySet). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Contract violation backed by source citation from three seats; return 0L instead of null (or explicitly change the SPI Javadoc).

findings.claim: Incomplete fix: the three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) unguarded and NPE under the same concurrent-delete race.
findings.evidence: modelSupplier is LazyModel(this::getGroupModel), which returns null once the row is deleted (same root cause the patch guards at 274-275). Reachable from REST: GroupResource.java:179-180 getSubGroups -> group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1) on a cached adapter (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}/children). Reasoned; proposed repro: copy of the new test whose reader loops groups().group(parentId).getSubGroups(0,10,true) while parents are deleted.
findings.reason: Same root cause as the commit's stated intent ('accessing group concurrently'); guard all four delegations consistently (Stream.empty()/0L).

findings.claim: Regression test never joins the reader thread: assertion runs immediately after deletedAll.set(true), so an exception from an in-flight request can land after the assert, and the raw thread can outlive the test and hit the realm during cleanup.
findings.evidence: GroupTest.java:139 'new Thread(() -> {...}).start()' with no reference kept; :155 deletedAll.set(true); :157 assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) with no join. If a remove() throws, deletedAll is never set and the reader loops indefinitely.
findings.reason: Cheap and makes the regression guard trustworthy: keep the Thread, try/finally set the flag, join with timeout before asserting.

findings.claim: Test can pass vacuously: nothing asserts the reader completed any reads during the deletes, and reproduction is timing-dependent, so it may pass on unpatched code.
findings.evidence: No read counter or assertion on reader progress in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti (GroupTest.java:117-158); race window depends on scheduling.
findings.reason: Add a successful-read counter and assert > 0 alongside the join fix; same edit surface as the join finding.

findings.reason: Coverage for the sibling-overload fix should ride along with that fix.

findings.evidence: tests/utils/.../ApiUtil.java:53-59 getCreatedId asserts 201 and closes the response; GroupTest.java:122-134 duplicates it; the new 'import static ...Assertions.fail' at :97 exists only for this branch. About -9 lines.
findings.reason: Advisory, non-blocking simplification in test code. ponytail: replace loop body with groupUuuids.add(ApiUtil.getCreatedId(managedRealm.admin().groups().add(group))) and drop the fail import.

findings.claim: Reader thread catches only Exception; an Error thrown in the reader dies silently and the test still passes.
findings.reason: The reader only makes admin-client calls; the bug signal (InternalServerErrorException/ProcessingException) is a RuntimeException and is caught. Errors (OOM, linkage) are not the race under test, and once the thread is joined per the accepted finding the residual gap is negligible.
